findings.title: Same concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the paged/searched subgroup methods
findings.body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). Three sibling methods still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check: getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) at line 268. If the group was deleted concurrently, isUpdated() is false (the adapter was not invalidated), modelSupplier.get() returns null, and the call throws NullPointerException. This is the same race the PR claims to fix, so the issue is only partially resolved.

findings.title: Parent lookup can return null and is then dereferenced in the hierarchy builder
findings.body: At line 47 parentModel comes from session.groups().getGroupById(...) and can be null if the parent was deleted concurrently. It is then used unguarded: at line 51 in canView(parentModel) when admin permissions are disabled; at line 57 in toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full) when the parent is not yet in the map; and at line 60 in populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent), which calls group.getSubGroupsCount() whenever subGroupsCount is true, even when the parent was already in the map. Each of these is an NPE in the same concurrent-access scenario the PR targets. The PR edits this file (only removing an unused helper) but does not add a null check here.

findings.title: getAttributes and getSubGroups lack the null-supplier guard that getRoleMappings has
findings.body: getRoleMappings (lines 70-76) returns an empty set when the group supplier is null, with a comment about groups not being loaded. getAttributes (lines 66-68) and getSubGroups (lines 90-92) pass the supplier straight to DefaultLazyLoader. If the group has been deleted and the value is not yet loaded, the loader will call methods such as source.getAttributes() or source.getSubGroupsStream() on null. This reaches GroupAdapter.getAttributes, getFirstAttribute, getAttributeStream and getSubGroupsStream() (line 240) through the same concurrent-deletion race, and the PR does not guard it. This assumes the loader dereferences the supplied source without a null check, which the guard in getRoleMappings suggests.

findings.title: Missing group now yields null count while sibling paths throw IllegalStateException
findings.body: For a group deleted concurrently, getSubGroupsCount now silently returns null (line 275). In the invalidated path, isUpdated() at lines 73-74 throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") for the same situation, so the class handles concurrent deletion inconsistently. A null Long is also not a count, so any caller that unboxes the result (for example, comparing it with > 0) will still throw NullPointerException. The change moves the NPE rather than defining the contract for a missing group.

findings.title: Reader thread is not joined before the assertion, and not stopped on failure
findings.body: The reader thread (lines 139-149) is never joined. The assertion at line 157 runs right after deletedAll.set(true) at line 155, so any exception from a read still in flight when the flag is set is never checked, and the test can pass despite an NPE. Also, the flag is set only on the happy path. If remove() at line 153 throws, deletedAll is never set, the reader loops forever against the server on a non-daemon thread, and the test fails without cleanup. Wrap the deletions in try/finally that sets the flag and joins the thread before asserting.

findings.title: Test depends on timing and does not deterministically reproduce the NPE
findings.body: The NPE is a race between a group lookup and a concurrent deletion. The test only has a chance to catch it if the reader thread happens to hit the window while groups are being removed. It can pass on unfixed code, and nothing targets getSubGroupsCount or the subgroup overloads specifically. A deterministic regression test, for example a run-on-server test that obtains a group adapter, deletes the group in another session, and then calls getSubGroupsCount and getSubGroupsStream, would show the fix works and would cover the other unguarded paths.
